name: Fright Fest at Six Flags Magic Mountain
summary: Six Flags Magic Mountain runs Fright Fest on select nights through November 1, 2026. Park admission covers the nighttime scare zones and shows; haunted mazes require a separate Haunted Attractions Pass. The park also offers Tricks and Treats for families during the day.
h1: Fright Fest at Six Flags Magic Mountain: what it is and whether it is worth it
title: Fright Fest Six Flags Magic Mountain
description: Six Flags Magic Mountain Fright Fest 2026 dates, admission and maze-pass costs, adult scares and daytime family options.

typicalWindow.hours: 6:30 p.m. to park closing on 2026 event nights

notes: Regular park admission or a valid pass covers Fright Fest scare zones and shows on scheduled nights, but not haunted mazes.
A 2026 single-night Haunted Attractions Pass starts at $25 and does not include park admission.
The park lists a combined admission-and-maze bundle from $74; prices vary by date and taxes or processing fees can apply.
Fright Fest starts at 6:30 p.m. on listed nights. Re-entry is not permitted after 9 p.m.

whatYouGet: Scare zones and roaming actors after dark on scheduled Fright Fest nights.
Seasonal entertainment and Halloween atmosphere included with park admission.
Access to operating rides under ordinary park admission, subject to closures and hours.
A separate daytime family event, Tricks and Treats, on its own published schedule.
whatYouDont: Haunted maze entry with a regular ticket or pass; the 2026 Haunted Attractions Pass is extra.
A promise that every ride operates during Fright Fest; check current ride closures and park hours.
A scare-free evening for young children; Six Flags does not recommend Fright Fest for guests under 13.

verdict.short: Worth considering for a coaster day that continues into nighttime scare zones. Budget for a separate maze pass if haunted houses are the point of your visit.
worthItIf: You want coasters and included scare zones on the same park visit.
Your group enjoys the after-dark atmosphere recommended for ages 13 and up.
You are willing to buy the maze add-on if haunted houses matter.
skipIf: You expect haunted mazes to come with standard admission.
Your group needs a scare-free evening; choose Tricks and Treats during the day.
The park calendar does not list Fright Fest on your available date.

strategy.heading: Choose the exact night
body: The published range is not a nightly calendar. Check the park’s date-specific operating calendar before buying travel or tickets.

strategy.heading: Price the mazes before you go
body: If you want haunted mazes, compare a Haunted Attractions Pass plus admission with the admission-and-maze bundle. Starting prices vary by date and may exclude fees.

strategy.heading: Use the daytime family event
body: Tricks and Treats offers less frightening Halloween activities before Fright Fest. Plan family activities first and leave before the night scares if younger guests are uncomfortable.

faqs.q: Is Fright Fest included with admission?
faqs.a: The scare zones and shows are available with park admission on scheduled Fright Fest nights. Haunted mazes in 2026 require a separate Haunted Attractions Pass. Check the park’s current ticket terms for your selected date.

faqs.q: When does Fright Fest run in 2026?
faqs.a: The park has announced select nights from September 18 through November 1, 2026. The range does not mean nightly operation; check the official park calendar for the exact date and hours of your visit.

faqs.q: Is Fright Fest suitable for young children?
faqs.a: Six Flags does not recommend the after-dark event for children under 13. The park also runs Tricks and Treats as a daytime, family-focused option on separately published dates.

faqs.q: Do I need a maze pass?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want to enter the 2026 haunted mazes. A normal park ticket or pass covers the general Fright Fest atmosphere but not maze admission. Check the park’s ticket page for current pass prices and fees.
